standard.title: Read and write high-frequency words
standard.description: read and write an increasing number of high-frequency words
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can spell one- and two-syllable words with common letter patterns (AC9E1LY13). They have also been building a high-frequency word bank at Foundation level. They have not yet expanded this bank to the growing range expected at Year 1, including irregular high-frequency words.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students read and write an increasing number of high-frequency words, including irregular forms.

nodes.label: Reading high-frequency words automatically
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can read an increasing number of high-frequency words automatically, without sounding out.
nodes.minimum_width: Read at least 20 Year 1-level high-frequency words automatically (at a glance, without decoding).
nodes.typical_width: Read an increasing bank of high-frequency words automatically when encountered in continuous text, including words with irregular phoneme-grapheme relationships (e.g. 'one', 'have', 'pretty').
wider: Read high-frequency words in varied sentence contexts — confirming they are recognised regardless of surrounding text
Identify high-frequency words in shared reading texts and discuss which are decodable and which need to be memorised
nodes.hinge_reason: Automatic high-frequency word recognition is a direct prerequisite for reading fluency — students who must decode common words cannot achieve the phrasing and pace needed for comprehension; their decoding load remains cognitively full on low-information words.

response_modes.reason: High-frequency word recognition is built through repeated exposure — seeing and reading words frequently until they are stored as sight words. Consolidation through wide reading and word-level practice is the primary lever.

success_criteria: Student reads target high-frequency words automatically (without phoneme-by-phoneme decoding)
Student recognises high-frequency words in continuous text as well as in isolation

nodes.label: Writing high-frequency words correctly
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can write high-frequency words correctly, including irregular forms, in their own writing.
nodes.minimum_width: Correctly spell at least 15 Year 1-level high-frequency words from memory in a writing context.
nodes.typical_width: Write an increasing bank of high-frequency words correctly in continuous writing, applying memory for irregular forms rather than phonetic attempts.
wider: Identify and self-correct misspelled high-frequency words in draft writing
Discuss why some high-frequency words cannot be spelled from phonics alone — building awareness of the need to memorise irregular forms
nodes.hinge_reason: Incorrect spelling of high-frequency words in independent writing signals that phonics-only strategies are being applied to irregular forms — this produces persistent misspellings that, once habituated, become difficult to correct.

response_modes.reason: Writing high-frequency words correctly requires memory, not just recognition. Students who can read a word may not yet reproduce it correctly from memory — repeated writing practice builds accurate production.

success_criteria: Student correctly spells at least 15 target high-frequency words in writing
Student's high-frequency word spelling is correct in independent writing contexts
